request:
I run a susu group at the market in Kumasi and I want to stop keeping the records in an exercise book. I need to start a group and add the members, each with their name and phone number. Every round, members pay in their contribution, and I record who paid, for which round, and how much in cedis. At the end of a round one member collects the pot, and the pot is everything that was paid in for that round, nothing more and nothing less. Each round has only one collector, and a member can collect only once, so if someone has already collected, they cannot collect again. Once a round has been collected, nobody can pay more into that round, and a round where nobody has paid anything cannot be collected. Contributions must be more than zero. For any member I want a statement showing how much they have paid in altogether and how much they have received. I also want to see the list of members and the collections made so far.

The client's answers to your questions:
Q: Does everyone pay the same fixed amount each round, or can each member pay any amount? Can a member pay more than once in the same round?
A: No, record whatever each member actually paid; the pot is the total paid in for that round.
Q: Can a round be collected once at least one person has paid, or must every member have paid first?
A: No preference: you decide.
Q: Are rounds simply numbered 1, 2, 3 and so on? Must they be collected in that order, or can people pay into and collect a later round before an earlier one is finished?
A: No preference: you decide.

Where the client has no preference or did not answer, choose the simplest option and add nothing they did not ask for (no logins, PINs or extra required fields).
summary:
I've built your susu records app in one file, `app.py`. It keeps everything in a small database file called `susu.db` in the same folder. I wrote 9 automatic checks that cover every rule you asked for, and they all pass. I didn't start the server and try it by hand, so the automatic checks are the only testing so far.

**What you can do (the endpoints):**
- **`POST /groups`**: start a group with a name.
- **`POST /groups/{groupId}/members`**: add a member with their name and phone number. Both are required.
- **`GET /groups/{groupId}/members`**: see the list of members.
- **`POST /groups/{groupId}/rounds/{roundNumber}/payments`**: record a payment by giving the member's number and the amount in cedis, e.g. `{"member_id": 1, "amount": 20.50}`.
- **`POST /groups/{groupId}/rounds/{roundNumber}/collection`**: record who collects the pot, e.g. `{"member_id": 1}`. The system works out the pot itself as the exact total paid into that round, so nobody can type in a different amount.
- **`GET /groups/{groupId}/collections`**: see the collections so far: round, who collected (number and name) and the pot.
- **`GET /groups/{groupId}/members/{memberId}/statement`**: see how much a member has paid in altogether and how much they have received.

**What gets refused:**
- **Missing details:** a member with no name or no phone number, or a group with no name.
- **Bad amounts:** a payment of zero or less, or one with more than 2 places after the decimal point (e.g. 5.555).
- **Bad round numbers:** zero, negative, or not a whole number.
- **Wrong group:** a payment or collection for someone who isn't in that group. A statement only works for members of that group.
- **Paying into a finished round:** no more payments once a round has been collected.
- **Collecting an empty round:** a round nobody has paid into can't be collected.
- **Two collectors:** only one person can collect each round.
- **Collecting twice:** a member who has already collected can't collect again.

Where you had no preference, I kept the simplest choices from the plan: rounds are numbered 1, 2, 3 and can be collected in any order, and a round can be collected once at least one person has paid. If someone pays twice in a round, both payments count towards the pot.

I added three limits you didn't ask for, to stop very large numbers from crashing the app:
- **Round numbers:** up to 1,000,000.
- **Payments:** up to 1 billion cedis each.
- **Name and phone length:** names up to 200 characters, phone numbers up to 50.

I also made sure that if two people record things at the same moment, the rules still hold. For example, two people can't both collect the same round.

plan.summary:
This plan replaces your exercise book for running a susu group. You can start a group, add members with their name and phone number, record each payment (who paid, for which round, and how many cedis), and record who collects the pot at the end of a round. The pot is always worked out by the system as the exact total paid into that round, so nobody can type in a different amount. You can also see a statement for any member, the list of members, and the collections made so far.

Where you had no preference, I chose the simplest options:
- Rounds are just numbered 1, 2, 3 and so on.
- Rounds do not have to be collected in order.
- A round can be collected as soon as at least one person has paid into it. Not every member has to pay first.
- Each member pays whatever amount they actually pay.
- If a member pays more than once in the same round, each payment is recorded and all of them count towards the pot.

Questions for you (none of these are in the plan unless you ask):
- Should anyone be able to see members' phone numbers, or should they be kept private?
- Do you need a way to correct or remove a payment that was entered by mistake?
- Would you like the date of each payment and collection to be recorded?

data.name: Collection
fields: pot amount in cedis (worked out automatically as the total paid into that round)

endpoints.does: Starts a new susu group with a name.
Adds a member to the group with their name and phone number.
Shows the list of all members in the group.
Records that a member paid an amount in cedis into this round.
Records which member collects the pot for this round. The pot is the total of everything paid into the round.
Shows all collections made so far: the round, who collected, and how much.
Shows a member's statement: how much they have paid in altogether and how much they have received.

rules: A member must have a name and a phone number.
A payment must be more than zero cedis.
A round number must be a whole number of 1 or more.
Payments and collections can only be made by members of that group.
A payment cannot be recorded for a round that has already been collected.
A round with no payments in it cannot be collected.
Each round can have only one collector. A second collection for the same round is refused.
A member who has already collected cannot collect again, in any round.
The pot is always the exact total paid into that round. It cannot be set to any other amount.
